text:
maria: Quick heads-up, I ran into an inconsistent import failure when folks use Poetry editable installs for the Python SDK. Repro: in the sample app run `poetry install` then `python -c 'import redwood_sdk; import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` -> ModuleNotFoundError for redwood_sdk.asyncio. Wheel builds in CI look fine.

sam: That sounds like the PEP 660/editable backend issue. Poetry's editable mode has tripped over package discovery before if pyproject metadata doesn't match disk layout. Can you paste pyproject.toml?

maria: Minimal pyproject: `[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"` We have normal layout with `redwood_sdk/__init__.py` and subpackages `asyncio/` and `typing/`. `pip wheel .` contains subpackages, but `poetry install` editable puts only the root package file into the environment. Behavior differs between machines.

josh: First checks: ensure not using implicit namespace packages (PEP 420) and confirm Poetry/core version — older Poetry had editable regressions.

maria: Not using namespace packages; all subdirs have __init__.py.

sam: Run `python -c "import redwood_sdk, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.walk_packages(redwood_sdk.__path__)))"` and `pip show -f redwood-sdk` in both envs to see installed files.

maria: In Poetry env pkgutil lists only the root; pip show -f outputs just `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`. `pip install -e .` works and shows everything.

dev-bot: CI job #6912 failed on macos-arm with "Invalid wheel tag for platform" (likely unrelated) https://ci.example/6912

josh: Workaround: make packaging explicit in pyproject. Use the `tool.poetry.packages` table or `include` globs, e.g.: `[tool.poetry.packages]
include = "redwood_sdk"` or under `[tool.poetry]` add `include = ["redwood_sdk/**","py.typed"]`. Also ensure `py.typed` is included so typing consumers and some installers don't prune files.

katie: Another practical workaround for contributors: `pip install -e .` (setuptools editable) or `poetry build && pip install dist/*.whl` to match CI. But we should fix metadata.

maria: I'll open a small PR to change pyproject to explicit packages + include `py.typed`. I'll also add a brief contributing note about editable quirks.

sam: Note: prefer explicit `[tool.poetry.packages]` table instead of inline `packages = [...]` since behavior varied across Poetry versions. Also run `poetry self update`.

josh: Add a CI smoke test that runs `poetry install` in a clean venv and asserts `python -c 'import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` to prevent regressions.

katie: I'll draft a dev onboarding doc mentioning preferred dev flows (we recommend `pip install -e .` for local dev, but document how to use Poetry). I'll also add the smoke test to CI.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/1332 (explicit [tool.poetry.packages] include, add py.typed to include list, update contributing docs). Please review.

josh: Reviewing now. If some contributors still see missing subpackages after merge, get minimal repro env details and we'll make a tiny sample repo to reproduce.

maria: Thanks all — will follow up if anything else shows up.
